Rossinavi's New Alfa Superyacht Boasts Sporty Styling and an Automotive-Inspired Bow Shield
8 photos
Photo: Rossinavi
There is nothing that screams luxury more than a custom superyacht. Designed as floating sanctuaries with every detail, from the naval architecture to interior materials and onboard amenities, dictated by the owner, bespoke superyachts are the ultimate expression of luxury on the open seas.
One of the leading shipyards known for turning bold visions into reality is Rossinavi, and the 62-meter (203-foot) full-custom Alfa superyacht is a great example of the Italian shipyard’s exceptional nautical craftsmanship.
Alfa is the latest custom creation launched by Rossinavi at its facilities in Viareggio and is the result of a collective effort between Fulvio De Simoni Yacht Design, which penned the exterior, Arrabito Naval Architect, which took care of naval architecture, and Omega Interior Design and Architecture for the interior.
Created as a one-off project for a client represented by Karma Yachting throughout the construction process, the vessel hit the water on November 25. It’s a full-displacement superyacht with a steel hull and aluminum superstructure that combines a sporty exterior with generous outdoor spaces, and a layout designed around privacy and onboard comfort.
Photo: Rossinavi Rossinavi is known for blending Italian naval architecture and interior craftsmanship with bold exterior lines, frequently drawing inspiration from automotive design, and this is also the case with Alfa. The vessel stands out with a sporty silhouette with dynamic lines, but its defining feature is an automotive-inspired bow shield, which incorporates a pronounced ridge and lights. Apart from acting as a starting point for the sporty appearance, it also gives the forward section of the yacht a truly distinctive look.
Like a true contemporary yacht, Alfa features ample glazing surfaces, but the windows on its lower and main decks feature a hull-colored treatment that makes the blend with the surrounding surface, creating the appearance of a continuous hull with no openings. The same approach to design consistency extends to the bulwarks, swimming pool, and outdoor furniture.
Another standout feature is the aft mezzanine deck, which acts as a link between the main and upper deck spaces while also shielding the main deck cockpit from the stern views and creating a sense of privacy. Designed to provide a seamless connection with the sea, the beach club opens through both aft and lateral openings, which connect with the swim platform to form a continuous space for spending time close to the water.
Photo: Rossinavi With a maximum beam of 11.1 meters (36.4 feet) and an interior volume of 1,210 GT, Alfa provides generous living quarters. It can accommodate up to 12 guests in six cabins, including two VIP cabins on the main deck and three guest staterooms below. Crew quarters provide space for 13 people across seven cabins.
The upper deck is home to a private owner’s apartment, which is designed as a retreat with its own outdoor area featuring a Jacuzzi, lounge seating and a sunbathing area. The sky lounge is a versatile space that can either remain part of the owner’s private quarters when desired or be opened for shared guest use on other occasions.
An al-fresco dining area on the same deck can be enclosed by sliding panels, transforming into a veranda with a dedicated heating and cooling system. This means it’s a space that can be enjoyed in any season.
Photo: Rossinavi Wellness facilities could not miss from a yacht designed for relaxation, entertainment, and comfort on the water. Alfa comes with several wellness amenities, including a massage room on the lower deck, a sauna near the beach club, and a gym at the aft end of the bridge deck. The custom yacht also has an observation deck, which offers another place for outdoor relaxation, with lounge seating, sunbathing areas, and panoramic views.
“The high standards of quality and design achieved with Alfa are the result of a close collaboration between Rossinavi and the Owner,” said Federico Rossi, Chief Operating Officer of Rossinavi. “From the very beginning, we have shared a common vision, working together to bring this project to life and achieve a result that reflects our mutual aspirations and expectations.”
Details regarding Alfa”s propulsion system and maximum and cruising speeds have not yet been disclosed. The superyacht’s delivery is scheduled for March 2027.
